X.note: Strong backlit light and a haze-filled lane that reads as a convincing rendered street. The soldiers are flat, blocky, cut-out-like figures. Their uniforms are mostly red with white cross-belts, so they look generic. A barefoot, bare-chested figure in a kilt-like garment stands at centre, which looks odd. Foreground barrels and rubble help the depth. Figures are sparse and fairly well separated, so the silhouettes stay readable.

Y.note: Same environment and lighting. The soldiers are packed into a dense mass of identical, stiff, game-asset figures with identical poses and no individual variation. Blue-coated troops (Hanoverian or artillery?) add some colour variety. The lane is cluttered and the figures merge into the background, and scale and perspective look slightly off. The light-up of the sea and ships in the distance is nice, and the open sky gives a cleaner top half.

why: X has the same strong set but fewer, better-separated figures that read more clearly and look less like a copy-pasted crowd of game assets, whereas Y's dense identical mass looks more toy-like.
top_fix_for_weaker: Reduce the crowd in Y and vary the soldiers' poses, heights, uniforms and spacing. Replace the cut-out figures with properly modelled, textured characters with believable cloth, faces and gear, and add contact shadows, dust and atmospheric haze so they sit in the lane.
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack with a thin St Patrick's cross, which is 1801 and later; in 1782 it would be the 1606 Union flag
Shuttered, weathered stone buildings look more Mediterranean-Victorian than 1782 siege-damaged Gibraltar, with intact rooftops and no bombardment damage
Bare-chested, kilt-like figure in X is out of place
Uniform cut and cross-belts look generic rather than 1782 specific, with flat bicorne or tricorne shapes
